[FIRRTL][InferDomains] Don't Infer Domains for Constants
items.body:
I'm starting to run into issues where the limited support for constants in `InferDomains` is causing domain inference errors.  Consider the following circuit:

``` firrtl
FIRRTL version 7.0.0
circuit Foo:

  domain ClockDomain:

  public module Foo:
    input A: Domain of ClockDomain
    output a: UInt<1> domains [A]
    input B: Domain of ClockDomain
    output b: UInt<1> domains [B]

    node x = UInt<1>(1)

    connect a, x
    connect b, x
```

This will presently fail domain inference due to the use of the node:

```
# firtool -domain-mode=infer circt/domain-constant-expression.fir
circt/domain-constant-expression.fir:15:5: error: illegal domain crossing in operation between operands b and x
    connect b, x
    ^
circt/domain-constant-expression.fir:15:5: note: see current operation: "firrtl.matchingconnect"(%arg3, %1) : (!firrtl.uint<1>, !firrtl.uint<1>) -> ()
circt/domain-constant-expression.fir:10:12: note: b has domains [B : ClockDomain]
    output b: UInt<1> domains [B]
           ^
circt/domain-constant-expression.fir:12:5: note: x has domains [A : ClockDomain]
    node x = UInt<1>(1)
    ^
circt/domain-constant-expression.fir:9:11: note: input module port B declared here
    input B: Domain of ClockDomain
          ^
circt/domain-constant-expression.fir:7:11: note: input module port A declared here
    input A: Domain of ClockDomain
          ^
```

I had originally thought that this could be made to work with an improvement to the constant checking in the pass.  However, this is fraught with difficulty as the constant-ness needs to propagate like a domain.

In the past, there's been discussions of an "empty" or "colorless" domain that may fit here.  Essentially, there exists a domain that things can be put into which can be used by any other domain, but does not unify with that domain.  In the above example, this would mean that the constant one and the node would be put into this domain.  This would then be allowed to be used by both the `A` and `B` domains, but would not unify with them.

The reason for the complication is that this needs to work through things like primops.  The above example is reduced from what I was seeing internally where this was actually:

``` firrtl
when eq(UInt<1>(0), UInt<1>(0)) : 
  ; body
```

Relatedly, any kind of CSE can create problems here, even if they didn't exist in the input circuit.

items.title: [FIRRTL] Width Inference Doesn't Support Domain Casts
items.body:
Consider the following:

``` firrtl
FIRRTL version 7.0.0
circuit Foo:
  domain ClockDomain:

  public module Foo:
    input A: Domain of ClockDomain
    input B: Domain of ClockDomain

    wire a: UInt domains [A]
    wire b: UInt<1> domains [B]
    wire c: UInt<1> domains [A]
    invalidate c

    connect b, unsafe_domain_cast(a, B)
    connect a, c
```

When running this through `firtool`, this will cause `InferWidths` to error out because it hasn't been taught about domain casts:

``` console
# firtool build/circt/domain-cast-width-inference.fir
build/circt/domain-cast-width-inference.fir:14:35: error: 'firrtl.unsafe_domain_cast' op not supported in width inference
    connect b, unsafe_domain_cast(a, B)
                                  ^
build/circt/domain-cast-width-inference.fir:14:35: note: see current operation: %4 = "firrtl.unsafe_domain_cast"(%0, %arg1) : (!firrtl.uint, !firrtl.domain<@ClockDomain()>) -> !firrtl.uint
```

This should be pretty straightforward to have `InferWidths` look through these casts.

[FIRRTL][circt-reduce] Remove TieOffCache for Invalid
items.body:
The `TieOffCache` creates problems for reductions involving domains.  This is because it is inherently incorrect as one invalid value must map to the same value.  For domains, this causes domain inference to treat a single invalid as having to be on exactly one domain which then unifies all users.  Again, it's fine that this is incorrect (as it's a reduction), however, this is creating a lot of false reductions in `circt-reduce`.

Unless there is a strong need for it, remove the `TieOffCache`'s `invalid` and have all reduction passes create unique invalids.

items.title: [FIRRTL] Get `-fixup-eicg-wrapper` working with domains
items.body:
The following circuit fails to compile when using the `-fixup-eicg-wrapper` option which will convert the `EICG_wrapper` janky external module to an intrinsic. This flow doesn't appear to be load bearing except for some internal things. However, it needs to work.

Consider:

``` firrtl
FIRRTL version 7.0.0
circuit Foo:
  domain ClockDomain:

  extmodule EICG_wrapper :
    input in : Clock
    input test_en : UInt<1>
    input en : UInt<1>
    output out : Clock
    input A : Domain of ClockDomain
    input B : Domain of ClockDomain
    defname = EICG_wrapper

  public module Foo:
    input A : Domain of ClockDomain
    input B : Domain of ClockDomain
    input in : Clock domains [A]
    input test_en : UInt<1> domains [A]
    input en : UInt<1> domains [A]
    output out : Clock domains [B]

    inst gate of EICG_wrapper
    connect gate.in, in
    connect gate.test_en, test_en
    connect gate.en, en
    connect out, gate.out
```

When compiled, this errors as intrinsic modules can't have domain ports:

``` console
# firtool Foo.fir -fixup-eicg-wrapper -mlir-print-ir-after-failure -domain-mode=infer-all
Foo.fir:5:3: error: 'firrtl.int.generic' op operand #4 must be variadic of a passive base type (contain no flips), but got '!firrtl.domain<@ClockDomain()>'
  extmodule EICG_wrapper :
  ^
Foo.fir:5:3: note: see current operation: %5 = "firrtl.int.generic"(%0, %2, %1, %3, %4) <{intrinsic = "circt_clock_gate", parameters = []}> : (!firrtl.clock, !firrtl.uint<1>, !firrtl.uint<1>, !firrtl.clock, !firrtl.domain<@ClockDomain()>) -> !firrtl.clock
```

While it is likely reasonable that intrinsics need domains, it's not necessary given that the domain information can be carried in other ops and the connections to these can be handled with casts. I'm planning to explore this approach for this one lowering and see how it works.

items.title: [domaintool][OM] Assertion failure when bouncing through extra object
items.body:
I've got a failure when using `domaintool` with the following example. This is likely a general bug (that I introduced) in the OM evaluator:

``` mlir
om.class @Domain(%in: !om.string)  -> (out: !om.string) {
  om.class.fields %in : !om.string
}
om.class @Foo_Class(%basepath: !om.frozenbasepath)  -> (test: i1) {
  %0 = om.constant "A" : !om.string
  %1 = om.object @Domain(%0) : (!om.string) -> !om.class.type<@Domain>
  %2 = om.object.field %1, [@out] : (!om.class.type<@Domain>) -> !om.string
  %3 = om.object @Domain(%2) : (!om.string) -> !om.class.type<@Domain>
  %4 = om.object.field %3, [@out] : (!om.class.type<@Domain>) -> !om.string
  %5 = om.constant "B" : !om.string
  %6 = om.prop.eq %4, %5 : !om.string
  om.class.fields %6 : i1
}
```

Running this, I hit an assertion:

``` console
# ./build/bin/domaintool ./build/Foo.reduced.mlir -module Foo
Assertion failed: (detail::isPresent(Val) && "dyn_cast on a non-existent value"), function dyn_cast, file Casting.h,
line 656.
zsh: abort      domaintool Foo.reduced.mlir -module Foo
```

The problem is that in `ReferenceValue::getStrippedValue`, while this is walking backwards, eventually this hits a
`currentValue.get()` which is nullptr:

```
(lldb) frame select 5
frame #5: 0x000000010339faa0
domaintool`circt::om::evaluator::ReferenceValue::getStrippedValue(this=0x000000010f30de58) const at Evaluator.h:136:22
   133    FailureOr<EvaluatorValuePtr> getStrippedValue() const {
   134      llvm::SmallPtrSet<ReferenceValue *, 4> visited;
   135      auto currentValue = value;
-> 136      while (auto *v = dyn_cast<ReferenceValue>(currentValue.get())) {
   137        // Detect a cycle.                                                                                          138        if (!visited.insert(v).second)                                                                              139          return failure();
(lldb) print currentValue.get()                                                                                        (std::shared_ptr<circt::om::evaluator::EvaluatorValue>::element_type *) nullptr                                        (lldb) print currentValue
(circt::om::evaluator::EvaluatorValuePtr) nullptr {                                                                      pointer = nullptr                                                                                                    }
```

If I remove the second `om.object`, then everything works.
